text: Almost every lake you see in Bengaluru was built by hand over 1,100 years, then the city lost most of them.
So why build lakes at all? Look at the map.
Bengaluru sits on a ridge about 920 meters up. No big river flows here. Rivers run downhill.
Bengaluru is the hill. So how do you fill lakes with no river?
Rewind to the 800s. People built earth walls across the valleys to trap the rain. Rain
fills one lake. It spills into the next. Then, the next. Wheee! Lake number seven!
Canals linked them into six chains, stepping down three valleys. In 1537, Kempe Gowda founded
the city and kept building more. Then the city grew and grew and grew. From 1973 to 2013,
about 79% of its water bodies vanished. So today, water is pumped about 100 kilometers
from the Kaveri and lifted 300 meters uphill. The city that built its own lakes now borrows
river. And the Lost Lakes? Many are hiding in plain sight. Kontirava Stadium? Sampangi
Lake. KR Market? Siddikate Lake. Majestic Bus Stand? Dharmambudi Lake. Technically,
I'm parked in a lake. Bengaluru never had a big river, so it made lakes instead.
This is Boogal. Follow for more geography fun facts.
